clue.text: Bad news, dear, it must be acknowledged

indicators.note: bad news is spoilt or wrecked, so the letters of the two words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone must admit to a loved one that there is unwelcome news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' seems to describe the news but is the anagram signal for the eight letters of NEWS DEAR; 'it must be' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer a letter or greeting is to acknowledge it, so the past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: A short reassurance that needn't be mentioned?

definitions.text: A short reassurance that needn't be mentioned?

parts.words: A short reassurance that needn't be mentioned?
parts.note: the polite brief reply to thanks, meaning 'don't mention it', read as a reassurance that the favour needn't be mentioned

explanation.surface: A quick word of comfort that is best left unsaid.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock polite response to thanks, equivalent to saying the matter needn't be mentioned.

clue.text: Marvellously impressed

parts.note: being struck with marvel, in other words filled with amazement

explanation.surface: Someone is greatly moved by a spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound adjective means struck with wonder or amazement, being impressed to the point of marvelling.

clue.text: Old magistrates, unusually severe

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual way, so the letters of severe are set out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Magistrates of old were known for harsh sentences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges SEVERE. A reeve was a medieval English local official with magisterial duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeves were historical English officials such as shire-reeves who administered justice locally.

clue.text: Herb makes many sick

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number, hence many
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A certain herb causes lots of people to be unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Using a Roman numeral for 'many' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is a feathery aromatic culinary herb, an example of the category.

clue.text: Bound to be short of cash

definitions.meaning: informal sense of being hard up, lacking money

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fastened with a strap and, colloquially, lacking money.

clue.text: Thought I'd half of each

parts.note: the contraction gives its letters without the apostrophe

indicators.note: half of means only the first two of the four letters of each are used

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that they would take a share of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought and a notion or concept are synonyms in the noun sense.

clue.text: A literary supplement?

parts.note: looks like a newspaper's books section but means an extra section appended to a written work

explanation.surface: A review section in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is an addition appended to a book or document, a supplement to the text.

clue.text: Fiancée at home and cared for

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
tended means looked after or cared for

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be is staying in and being looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one is engaged to marry, a fiancée or fiancé.

clue.text: Kind of gun having catches reversed

indicators.note: reversed tells us to read the word for catches from right to left

parts.note: nets means catches, as fish in a net

explanation.surface: A firearm whose safety catches have been put on backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' looks like a gun part but is a verb, NETS, which 'reversed' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten is a British submachine gun of the Second World War, an example of a gun type.

clue.text: Reckless villain can show solicitude

parts.note: a devil is a wicked person, a villain
may means is permitted to, as can does informally
to care is to show concern or solicitude

explanation.surface: Even a scoundrel is capable of kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil-may-care attitude is cheerfully careless of consequences, which is to say reckless.

clue.text: Aunt reckons a doctor is bad-tempered

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aunt thinks a physician is grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb signalling the anagram of AUNT RECKONS A; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous means quarrelsome and irritable, a close synonym of bad-tempered.

clue.text: This sort of clue is included in the French game

indicators.note: included in means one word is placed within the other

parts.note: le is a French word for the
this clue is itself an across clue in the grid

explanation.surface: A clue type crops up in a sport played in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The self-referential 'This sort of clue' means an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, an example of a game.

clue.text: Doctor gets notes about implant

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the notes go round the doctor

parts.note: E, E and D are musical notes
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a qualification of a doctor

explanation.surface: A physician receives letters about a medical implant.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly in a surrounding mass, to implant it.

clue.text: What is written is enclosed

definitions.meaning: ... in the sense of set down with a pen
... in the sense of shut in a pen, like livestock

explanation.definitionFit: The verb pen means both to write and to confine in an enclosure, so the past participle carries both.

clue.text: Scheme for a small piece of ground

explanation.definitionFit: A plot is both a conspiratorial plan and a small parcel of land.

clue.text: Make light of Winnie's duplicity?

indicators.note: duplicity is read literally as doubling, so the bear's name appears twice

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the bear in A. A. Milne's stories, known as Pooh

explanation.surface: A children's bear is accused of deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duplicity' normally means deceit, but here it is taken as duplication.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh something is to dismiss it as unimportant, to make light of it.

clue.text: Listen out by employing devices initially -like ears?

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to use hearing aids when trying to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ears have lobes, so lobed describes something with rounded projections like an ear.

clue.text: Completely fail to provide breakfast?

definitions.meaning: informal phrase for a show or joke that flops
what a hen does to supply a breakfast item

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to flop badly, while literally a hen producing something for the breakfast table.

clue.text: A mother for the first fellow?

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, such as a horse

explanation.surface: The question of who mothered the very first man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam is the first man created, so he is literally the first fellow.

clue.text: Bill takes detectives to hospital department after crash

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Police take a man named Bill to hospital after a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but means an account. CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a kind of accident, typically involving vehicles.

clue.text: At work -though returning no tax

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the small word no is read backwards

parts.note: a duty is a tax, as on imports

explanation.surface: Someone working while their tax money comes back to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on duty means being engaged in one's work at that moment.

clue.text: Try to score in Rugby, but decline to put the boot in

parts.note: to drop is to fall or decline
to kick, literally to strike with one's boot

explanation.surface: A rugby player attempts points but refuses to resort to violent kicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like a rugby try but is the verb attempt; a drop-kick is a ball dropped and kicked as it bounces, used for a drop goal.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a drop-kick is a method of attempting to score a drop goal.

clue.text: Choose one Mother the best!

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral one
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An exhortation to pick Mum as the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Optima is the plural of optimum, the best or most favourable conditions.

clue.text: It allows time for paying standing charges

definitions.text: It allows time for paying standing charges

parts.words: It allows time for paying standing charges
parts.note: standing charges suggests utility bills, but means fees for a car standing in a bay for a paid time

explanation.surface: A billing system that gives extra time to pay fixed fees.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside coin machine sells time for a vehicle to remain parked in a space.

clue.text: Correct pronunciation for the ceremony

indicators.note: pronunciation tells us the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: right means correct

explanation.surface: How to say a word properly at a formal ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a ritual or formal religious ceremony.

clue.text: Floor coverings having a dull shine at first

parts.note: mat, also matt, means having a dull, non-glossy finish

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of shine is used

explanation.surface: Rugs that start out glossy before losing their sheen.
explanation.definitionFit: Mats are small pieces of material laid on a floor, a kind of floor covering.

clue.text: Duck on the German river

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, looking like O
der is German for the

explanation.surface: A duck floats on a river in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence O. The Oder forms part of the German-Polish border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a central European river, an example of the category.

clue.text: Rejected just for being unqualified

parts.note: out means rejected or no longer accepted
right means fair or just

explanation.surface: Someone is turned down simply for lacking qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unqualified' suggests lacking credentials but means absolute, without reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: An outright or unqualified success is complete and without reservation.

clue.text: Fresh pastry is in short supply

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Freshly baked pastry is hard to come by.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsity is scarcity or thinness of distribution, the state of being in short supply.
